chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hamza ibn Humran and Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, who both said: We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and there were some people with him. So he led them in the Asr prayer, and we had already prayed. We counted for him during his bowing, 'Glorious is my Lord the Magnificent', thirty-four or thirty-three times. And one of them said in his hadith: 'And his praise during the bowing and prostration was the same.' This is because he (peace be upon him) knew the capacity of the people for the length of his bowing and prostration, and that is because it is reported that the virtue for the Imam is to lighten [the prayer] and pray with the weakest of the people.

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ: Glorious is my Lord the Magnificent (recited in bowing)

ai.seo_question: How did the Imam determine the length of his prayer when leading a mixed congregation?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s (peace be upon him) sensitivity to the congregation's capacity, specifically noting that he balanced the length of bowing and prostration to avoid burdening them. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the Imam should lead according to the weakest member of the congregation, ensuring accessibility and ease in worship. The text also clarifies the equality of glorification in both postures, reflecting the holistic nature of physical devotion in prayer.
